parsed.why: Most protective state: bathroom ban absent, shield law aids out-of-state trans care, nondiscrimination and hate-crime recourse; national border/custody restrictions still suppress below safe.

Criminal universal exposure: state law makes any restroom/changing room mismatch a jailable offence, including private businesses and hospitals; litigation limits enforcement certainty but exposure remains severe.

Hostile rule enforced: police ID checks at capitol restrooms, school investigation, prison coverage, marker/care denial, no state recourse; top Do Not Travel under severe national entry/custody regime.
Deeply restrictive regime: school/state facility bans, binary legal sex, marker denial, adult care funding bans, minimal recourse; severe institutional denial even absent documented enforcement.

Above parent average: no current bathroom ban and local ordinances partially protect; but national border/custody, hostile care/document laws, no statewide recourse, and active legislative reversal risk remain.
